purpose: Upgrade the local rank-3 obstruction from one 2D-subspace model to the entire projected-delta-matroid gadget class. Projection of any delta-matroid is again a delta-matroid, while the five-state 2-vs-1 switch is not a delta-matroid. Therefore no number of existential hidden elements can turn one projected linear/delta-matroid gadget into the exact local switch relation.

local_relation.meaning: L,R are the two majority-sign occurrences and M is the minority-sign occurrence of one mixed degree-3 Boolean variable. The relation allows any majority subset or the minority singleton, but never both signs.

lemma_projection_preserves_delta.statement: Let D=(V union H,F) be any delta-matroid and define its existential projection to V by P={X subseteq V : exists A subseteq H with X union A in F}. Then (V,P) is a delta-matroid.
proof: Take projected feasible X,Y and choose lifts X union A and Y union B in F.
For u in X symmetric-difference Y, u also lies in the symmetric difference of the two lifts.

By the delta-matroid symmetric-exchange axiom in D, there exists v in (X symmetric-difference Y) union (A symmetric-difference B), possibly v=u, such that (X union A) symmetric-difference {u,v} is feasible.
If v is visible, projecting this feasible lift gives X symmetric-difference {u,v} in P.
If v is hidden, projecting gives X symmetric-difference {u} in P, which is exactly the allowed symmetric exchange with the second exchange element chosen equal to u.
lemma_projection_preserves_delta.literature_alignment: Projection of a delta-matroid is standard and remains a delta-matroid; projected linear delta-matroids are algorithmically studied, including Koana-Wahlstrom STACS 2025.

theorem.name: RANK3_2_VS_1_SWITCH_IS_NOT_A_PROJECTION_OF_ANY_DELTAMATROID
proof: The five-state relation R fails symmetric exchange: take X={L,R}, Y={M}, u=M. The only candidates are X symmetric-difference {M}={L,M,R}, X symmetric-difference {M,L}={M,R}, and X symmetric-difference {M,R}={L,M}; all are infeasible.
Hence R is not a delta-matroid.
By the projection lemma, if R were the existential projection of any delta-matroid with arbitrary hidden elements, then R itself would be a delta-matroid. Contradiction.
theorem.field_scope: Combinatorial; no field or characteristic assumption. In particular it excludes projected linear delta-matroid gadgets over every field.

killed: Represent one mixed degree-3 switch by one projected linear delta-matroid gadget, with any polynomial number of local hidden elements, then invoke linear/projected-linear delta-matroid parity/optimization.
Repair the local five-state defect merely by adding existential auxiliary ports inside a single delta-matroid and projecting them away.
not_killed: The v2.0 representation of the switch as the INTERSECTION of two projected-linear relations; intersection need not be a delta-matroid.
A global construction coupling many switches and clauses before projection, where no individual switch is represented as an isolated projected gadget.
A direct augmentation algorithm for the special three-way system.

next_target.name: E8_GLOBAL_TWO_PROJECTED_LINEAR_PLUS_CLAUSE_AUGMENTATION_V3_1
next_target.directive: Local projected-delta repair is forbidden. Work globally with the exact decomposition already available: two pair-equality projected-linear layers plus the clause partition/nonempty layer. Seek a single polynomial augmentation or obstruction theorem for their source-aligned interaction; do not collapse each rank-3 switch to one projected gadget.

sources: Koana and Wahlstrom, Faster Algorithms on Linear Delta-Matroids, STACS 2025.
Kakimura and Takamatsu, Matching Problems with Delta-Matroid Constraints, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2013.
